sections.label: Mental health appointment waiting times
sections.summary: A Parliamentary Question on mental health waiting times drew a Ministry reply of 45 days for a psychiatrist and 42 days for a psychologist.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A Parliamentary Question was filed in July this year by the hon Member Mr Yip Hon Weng on average waiting times and follow-up appointments for mental health treatment at public healthcare institutions, wherein the Ministry responded that, on the basis of median time, it takes 45 days to see a psychiatrist and 42 days to see a psychologist.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Depending on whether one sees it as half empty or half full, it means that 50% of all cases referred to see a psychiatrist or psychologist wait no less than six weeks before an appointment can be arranged.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Even, Mr Speaker, if we take a conservative and reasonably optimistic view that perhaps the remaining 50% are seen within eight weeks or by the second month from their referral, it is also worth noting that by the time patients need to be referred by the learned general practitioner to a psychiatrist or psychologist, it is likely the case that these patients are already struggling and are having marked difficulty in their lives.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would argue that a further six to eight weeks' wait for access to a psychiatrist and/or psychologist is much too long a wait to bear.

sections.label: Study insurance coverage exclusions
sections.summary: The speaker proposes the Government study the evidence and reasons for refusals, loading and exclusions in mental health insurance coverage.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My proposal, Mr Speaker, is for the Government to study this issue more deliberately and have a deeper look at the evidence and reasons for refusing, for loading and making exclusions for insurance coverage relating to mental health conditions.

sections.label: Healthier SG capacity expansion
sections.summary: The Government's Healthier SG push aims for 32 polyclinics by 2030 and 30% more public hospital capacity, with 500 beds added yesterday.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Sometimes, even with the best roads, jams can occur if intersections are not well-designed or if traffic junction timings are poorly thought through.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am heartened, Mr Speaker, that the Government has had a renewed push for Healthier SG, as espoused by its White Paper, with an aim of 32 polyclinics by 2030 and an increase of public hospital capacity by 30%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In fact, just yesterday, a further 500 beds were added to the healthcare system as the hon Minister for Health initiated the opening of the Tan Tock Seng Hospital Integrated Care Hub.

sections.label: Muslim community mental health experts
sections.summary: The Muslim community must raise awareness and encourage more people into psychology and psychiatry, as experts managing the issue are very few.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In line with that, the Muslim community must also focus sharply on raising awareness and encouraging more people to venture into the fields of psychology and psychiatry, because the number of experts managing this issue currently is very low.

sections.label: Bias and workplace fairness legislation
sections.summary: The speaker says his response starts from day-to-day biases, and welcomes MOM's August announcement on workplace fairness legislation for disability and mental health.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My response ordinarily revolves around the fact that it starts from our own day-to-day biases, how we respond organically and spontaneously to matters of mental health and how sensitive we are to what we read and what we hear of mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am particularly optimistic by the announcement by the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) in August regarding the upcoming workplace fairness legislation, especially in protecting against workplace discrimination for disability and mental health conditions.

sections.label: Urging Members on mental health care
sections.summary: The speaker urges Members to consider mental health, its accessibility, and vulnerable citizens' struggles for timely care and worries about employability.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I urge Members to consider your position on how you view issues related to mental health, its accessibility to care and how some of our citizens at their most vulnerable hour struggle to get timely accessible care, lack reasonable alternative options to support their needs and have valid worries about employability after.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is even higher than diabetes which stood at 9.5% in 2020 on whom we rightly wage war against since 2016.

sections.label: Poor mental health prevalence rise
sections.summary: The National Population Health Survey reported poor mental health prevalence among Singapore citizens rose from 13% in 2020 to 17% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The recent National Population Health Survey reported a rise in prevalence of poor mental health among Singapore citizens from 13% in 2020 to 17% in 2022.

sections.label: National Mental Health Strategy report
sections.summary: The Task Force reviewed the landscape, studied gaps, consulted the public and stakeholders, and put together a National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy, with a full report released in the next few days.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Over the past two years, the Task Force has reviewed the landscape, studied gaps and challenges and consulted the public and stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We have since put together a comprehensive National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy that charts our way forward to improve the mental health of Singaporeans, and we will be releasing a full report of the strategy in the next few days.

sections.label: Healthcare subsidies and MediShield Life
sections.summary: All Singaporeans are eligible for healthcare subsidies of up to 80% in public health care institutions, and all Singaporeans and permanent residents are covered under MediShield Life regardless of pre-existing conditions, including mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Today, all Singaporeans are eligible for healthcare subsidies of up to 80% in the public health care institutions and all Singaporeans and permanent residents are also covered under MediShield Life, regardless of pre-existing conditions, including mental health conditions.

sections.label: MAS action against insurers
sections.summary: MAS will take action against insurers whose practices breach its regulations or guidance, and individuals with concerns over underwriting decisions can appeal through insurers' feedback channels or MAS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) will take action against insurers whose practices are in breach of MAS' regulations or guidance and individuals with concerns over the insurers' underwriting decision can make an appeal through your insurers' feedback channel or through MAS.

sections.label: MOM and NCSS employment support
sections.summary: MOM, with NCSS, is looking into improving employment and employability of persons with mental health conditions and strengthening workplace mental well-being support, with more details in the National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The MOM, together with NCSS, is looking into improving the employment and employability of persons with mental health conditions and strengthening support for mental well-being at the workplace, such as better work life harmony strategies and more job opportunities for persons with mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: More details on these will be released in the National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy in the next few days.

sections.label: Sitting time change announcement
sections.summary: Pursuant to Standing Order 2(3)(a), the Sitting tomorrow will commence at 12.30 pm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Pursuant to Standing Order 2(3)(a), I wish to inform hon Members that the Sitting tomorrow will commence at 12.30 pm.
